outcome: Admission to the neonatal intensive care unit (ICU)
cohort: The study evaluated 204 newborns with gestational age between 34 and 36 weeks and six days, compared to 205 full-term newborns (39 and 40 weeks and six days), from a reference maternity hospital in northeastern Brazil.
finding: Late preterm infants exhibited significantly higher rates of hypothermia, hypoglycemia, respiratory distress syndrome, jaundice requiring phototherapy, NICU admission, difficulty breastfeeding, longer hospital stay, and mortality compared to full-term newborns.
gest_age: 34 to 36 weeks and six days (late preterm); 39 to 40 weeks and six days (full-term)
